meetings.title: CityLife: "FY'12 -13 Budget" (July August 2012)
meetings.executive_summary: In this CityLife television broadcast, host Beverly Thompson interviews City Manager Tom Bonfield regarding the City of Durham's recently adopted FY 2012-13 budget. Bonfield explains the inclusive budget development process and highlights key revenue and spending measures, including a dedicated one-cent property tax increase for affordable housing, a seven-cent Business Improvement District (BID) tax rate in downtown Durham, transit service enhancements, public safety investments, ongoing street-repaving funding, and a 2.7% water and sewer rate increase. No City Council votes or formal motions take place during this informational broadcast.

agenda_items.title: Budget Process and Dedicated One-Cent Property Tax Increase for Affordable Housing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Host Beverly Thompson and City Manager Tom Bonfield discuss the City's budget process, which began in February using resident satisfaction surveys, strategic plan priorities, and early City Council guidelines. Bonfield explains that while tax rates for general operations, debt, and transit remained unchanged, the budget includes a one-cent property tax increase (about $15 annually on a $150,000 home) strictly dedicated to affordable housing. The tax generates approximately $2.3 million per year to supplement declining federal HUD funding for physical housing production and neighborhood redevelopment.

agenda_items.title: Downtown Durham Business Improvement District (BID) Tax Rate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bonfield explains the seven-cent additional property tax rate for the Downtown Durham Business Improvement District (BID), adopted by the City Council at the urging of Downtown Durham Inc. and downtown property owners. The dedicated revenue—estimated at roughly $400,000 per year—is earmarked for enhancing downtown cleanliness, safety, appearance, friendliness, and marketing.

agenda_items.title: Bus System Enhancements and Regional Transit Sales Tax Referendum
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bonfield discusses the City Council-approved Better Bus System study conducted with Triangle Transit Authority and bus riders, marking the first comprehensive evaluation of Durham's bus system in 25 to 30 years. Within existing transit tax rates, the budget funds improved on-time performance and added capacity on crowded routes. He also notes that revenue from Durham County's November 2011 transit sales tax referendum remains on hold until Orange County—which is moving forward with a fall referendum—and Wake County take action to advance regional bus and light rail plans.

agenda_items.title: Public Safety Funding and Operation Bullseye Expansion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Citing resident satisfaction survey findings that over 80% of residents feel safe in Durham, Bonfield outlines public safety priorities in the FY 2012-13 budget. The budget maintains full police staffing, adds three firefighters to improve response times, continues joint warrant-control efforts with Durham County and funding for a dedicated domestic violence judge, and uses City funds to sustain Operation Bullseye in Northeast Central Durham while launching a smaller version in Southside.

agenda_items.title: Street Repaving Bond Progress and Ongoing Operating Revenue
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bonfield reports that the City is 25% to 27% ahead of schedule on spending the $20 million street-repaving bond referendum approved by voters two years earlier, with funds expected to be exhausted by the fall. To avoid relying solely on borrowing for recurring maintenance, the budget dedicates $750,000 in new ongoing operating funds to street resurfacing, with a long-term goal of building that annual allocation to $4 million to $5 million.

agenda_items.title: Water, Sewer, and Stormwater Rate Increases and Budget Transparency
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bonfield explains the 2.7% water and sewer rate increase ($1.26 per month for an average Tier 3 customer), noting that the enterprise system relies strictly on user fees rather than property taxes to replace aging infrastructure—such as century-old water lines along Main Street—and meet Falls Lake and Jordan Lake environmental compliance standards at water reclamation facilities. He closes by emphasizing fiscal transparency, resident satisfaction gains of roughly 25% over six years, and public access to budget documents via the City website.

meetings.title: FY'12-'13 Proposed Budget segment from ep. 139 of City Hall This Week
meetings.executive_summary: This segment from Episode 139 of City Hall This Week summarizes City Manager Tom Bonfield's proposed $372 million FY 2012-13 budget, which was presented to the Durham City Council on May 21, 2012. Highlights include a $176.6 million general fund, a property tax increase costing $15 annually on a $150,000 home dedicated to affordable housing, water/sewer and stormwater rate adjustments, $400,000 for neighborhood commercial revitalization, and a seven-cent tax rate for the Downtown Durham Business Improvement District. No formal motions or Council votes occur during this informational news segment, which notes a June 4 public hearing and June 18 final approval date.

agenda_items.title: Proposed $372 Million FY 2012-13 Budget and General Fund Public Safety Allocation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The segment introduces City Manager Tom Bonfield's proposed $372 million FY 2012-13 spending plan presented to the City Council on May 21, representing a $10 million overall increase from the prior year alongside a smaller $176.6 million general fund for core services. More than $80 million—or 45% of the general fund—is allocated to public safety across the police, fire, emergency communications, and emergency management departments.

agenda_items.title: Dedicated Property Tax Increase for Affordable Housing Initiatives
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The proposal includes a property tax increase that raises annual property taxes for the owner of a $150,000 home by $15.00 to establish a dedicated funding source for affordable housing initiatives. Remarks in the segment emphasize that dependable, affordable, quality housing stock is essential to thriving, livable neighborhoods across Durham.

agenda_items.title: Water, Sewer, and Stormwater Rate Adjustments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The proposed budget recommends average rate increases of about $1.26 per month for water and sewer charges and $5.40 per year for stormwater rates. Water and sewer revenues support operational and maintenance needs, while stormwater fee increases fund major capital projects required under the Falls Lake and Jordan Lake rules.

agenda_items.title: Neighborhood Commercial Revitalization, Downtown BID, and Adoption Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The proposed budget allocates an additional $400,000 for neighborhood commercial revitalization in targeted areas, building on $386,000 committed the prior year to two East Durham projects projected to leverage over $12 million in private investment and create 200 temporary and 38 full-time jobs. It also launches the Downtown Durham Business Improvement District with a seven-cent tax rate per $100 of assessed value for enhanced downtown services, with a public hearing scheduled for June 4 and final Council approval set for June 18.
